---
title: The configuration
description: The options of _quarto.yml that smalldocs reads, and the options that it adds.
order: 2
---

smalldocs reads `_quarto.yml` as Quarto does. An option is a key in `_quarto.yml`, in a `_metadata.yml`
file or in the front matter of a page. smalldocs merges the options in this order, and a later value
wins:

1. The top level and `format.html` of `_quarto.yml`.
2. A `_metadata.yml` file in each folder on the path to the page.
3. The front matter of the page.

If smalldocs does not read an option, the build gives a warning. With `smalldocs render --strict`, a
warning makes the build fail.

## project

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `type` | `website`. A `book` is built as a website, with its chapters as the sidebar. Another type stops the build |
| `output-dir` | The output folder; `_site` by default. See the note below the table |
| `render` | One glob, or a list of globs, of the pages to build. A glob that starts with `!` leaves pages out. Without `render`, every `.qmd`, `.md` and `.ipynb` file is a page |
| `resources` | One glob, or a list of globs, of more files to copy into the site, such as `.nojekyll` or `images/**` |
| `pre-render`, `post-render` | Commands to run before and after the build, in the folder of the project, with the `QUARTO_PROJECT_*` variables of Quarto |

Each build deletes the old content of the output folder. So smalldocs refuses an output folder in these
cases:

- The folder is the project, or a folder above the project.
- The folder holds a `.git` folder.
- The folder holds files, but no `site_libs` folder. A `site_libs` folder shows that an earlier build
  of Quarto or smalldocs made the folder.

Without `render`, smalldocs leaves out some files, as Quarto does. It leaves out files and folders whose
names start with `_` or `.`, the output folder, virtual environments and `README.md`.

## Globs

A glob is a path pattern, such as `guide/*.qmd`. smalldocs reads globs as Quarto does:

- In a glob with a `/`, the `*` stays inside one folder, and `**` crosses folders. So `guide/*` finds
  `guide/a.qmd`, but not `guide/old/b.qmd`. `guide/**` finds both.
- A glob with no `/`, such as `*.qmd`, finds files in every folder.
- A folder name, such as `guide/`, means the pages in the folder.

Sometimes a page links to a page that is not built, for example a draft. smalldocs reports the link,
and it never copies the source of that page into the site.

## website

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `title`, `description` | The name and the summary of the site |
| `site-url` | The address of the site. smalldocs needs it for `sitemap.xml` and for feeds |
| `repo-url`, `repo-branch`, `repo-subdir`, `repo-actions` | Links under the table of contents: `edit`, `source`, `issue` |
| `navbar` | `left`, `right`, `tools`, `title`, `logo`, `background`, `search`. An entry is a page, or `href` and `text`, with an `icon`. `menu` makes a dropdown |
| `sidebar` | `contents`, `style` (`floating` or `docked`), `title`, `logo`, `search`, `tools`, `collapse-level`. A list gives several sidebars |
| `page-navigation` | Links to the previous page and the next page of the sidebar |
| `page-footer` | One text, or `left`, `center` and `right`. Each part is Markdown or a list of entries |
| `search` | `false` turns search off |
| `favicon`, `open-graph`, `bread-crumbs` | The icon, the Open Graph tags and the breadcrumbs. `false` hides the breadcrumbs |

The `contents` of a sidebar takes the same entries as in Quarto:

```yaml
sidebar:
  contents:
    - index.qmd                      # a page
    - section: Guide                 # a section that folds
      contents: guide/*              # a glob: by `order:`, then the index page, then by path
    - section: Reference
      href: api/index.qmd            # a section that is also a page
      contents:
        - api/one.qmd
    - auto: examples                 # one section for each folder, titled by its index page
    - text: Elsewhere
      href: https://example.com
    - text: "---"                    # a line
```

## format.html, and the front matter of a page

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `theme` | A Bootswatch name, or `light:` and `dark:` for two themes and a toggle. See [Themes](themes.qmd) |
| `css` | Your stylesheets, after the stylesheet of the theme |
| `toc`, `toc-depth`, `toc-title` | The table of contents at the right of the page |
| `number-sections` | Numbers before the headings |
| `code-copy` | The copy button on code. It is on by default |
| `from` | The Pandoc reader, with extensions. smalldocs reads `-smart` and `-tex_math_dollars` |
| `page-layout` | `article` (the default), `full` or `custom` |
| `link-external-newwindow` | Open links to other sites in a new tab |
| `include-in-header`, `include-before-body`, `include-after-body` | Files, or `text:` entries, to put into each page |
| `echo`, `output`, `include`, `execute` | Hide the code or the output of every cell. `execute: {echo: false}` works too |
| `title`, `subtitle`, `description`, `author`, `date`, `date-format`, `categories`, `image` | The title block, and what a listing shows |
| `draft` | `true` leaves the page out of the site |
| `order` | The place of a page among the pages that a glob finds |
| `listing` | A list of other pages. See [Listings](listings.qmd) |
| `title-block-banner` | A band of the primary colour behind the title |

## smalldocs

Quarto ignores a top-level key that it does not know. So smalldocs keeps its own options under
`smalldocs:`, and Quarto can still build the same project.

```yaml
smalldocs:
  linkify: true          # a documented name in backticks links to its entry; on with `api`
  symbols: _symbols.json # the index of names that linkify reads
  api:                   # the API reference: see the API page
    packages: [mypkg]
```

Linkify is also on when `filters` lists a file with the name `linkify.lua`. Projects made for Quarto use
that filter, so such a project needs no change.
